title: Legacy Relationship Integration
definition: The process of incorporating legacy relationships into a dynamic knowledge graph to ensure a cohesive and accurate representation of concepts.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine you have a map with some details missing. To make the map more complete, you add in some extra details that were previously created for another map. This is similar to what we're doing with our knowledge graph.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Legacy relationship integration involves merging data from a static HTML file into a dynamic knowledge graph system. This ensures that the current graph reflects the full range of relationships, not just the ones generated by the live blockstore.
difficulty_levels.expert: The process of legacy relationship integration is a crucial step in creating a robust knowledge graph. It allows the system to incorporate previously curated data, enhancing its completeness and accuracy. This is particularly important in a dynamic system where the live blockstore may not yet have fully populated relationships. The integration should be done in a way that prioritizes the quality and relevance of the data, while also ensuring the system's scalability and performance.

extra_fields.insight: The old map was a hand-curated artifact, and the current system can benefit from integrating its relationships into the dynamic knowledge graph.
